results.title: Verdict week in the Myanmar genocide case
results.content: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 16: The international press looks ahead to a verdict that could find the state of Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority. In other news, French journalists lift the lid on the many trials involving child prostitution. And finally, in Ireland, a cache of 12,000 once-banned books is back in the spotlight.

results.title: Breaking taboos: Egypt's sexual revolution takes to social media
results.content: In Egypt, a sexual revolution is quietly unfolding on social media. Accounts followed by tens of thousands of people, with posts attracting millions of views, are tackling a wide range of issues surrounding sexuality – from the widespread practice of female genital mutilation (which 93 per cent of women in rural areas have undergone) to sex education and sexual pleasure.

results.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss 'world peace' at Shenzhen summit, China says
results.content: The Chinese foreign ministry on Monday said that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability" when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week. The meeting is expected to happen on Thursday on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders.

results.title: Nations League: France defeat Turkey to advance to quarter-finals
results.content: France struggled at times but defeated Turkey (2-1) in the Nations League matchday. France finished first in group A1 and qualified for the quarter-finals.

results.title: 🔴 Live: 600 Ukrainian drones target Moscow, Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
Live: 600 Ukrainian drones target Moscow, Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
results.content: Russian air defences intercepted 600 Ukrainian drones flying towards the Moscow region overnight and into Monday morning, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said. Ukraine also struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea across the Kerch straight, the peninsula's Russia-backed governor said. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.

results.title: Five EU nations set to announce migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda
results.content: Five EU countries on Monday are set to announce a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda – the first such facility outside the bloc. The move comes after the EU toughened its migration rules in late 2025.

results.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu ‘cannot remain’ after alleged election interference by aide
results.content: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. The former army chief called Netanyahu and his entourage an immediate threat to democracy, hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.

results.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over public media funding plan
results.content: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

results.title: Elon Musk, Uber co-founder join calls to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief
results.content: Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder were among more than 158,000 signatories by Sunday demanding Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief pending an independent investigation. Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a subordinate and another with a woman accused of spying for China, ending his 33-year tenure.

results.title: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, architect of Mexico’s drug trade, dies age 80
results.content: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.

results.title: Kroupi on target as France beat Turkey to reach Nations League quarters
results.content: Eli Junior Kroupi scored his maiden goal for France as Les Bleus beat Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux on Sunday to top their group with 13 points and qualify for the quarter-finals of the Nations League. World Cup winners Spain, who lost at home against England, are among their potential opponents in the last eight.

results.title: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in two days
results.content: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached the Canary Islands over the past two days, Spain’s coastguard said Sunday, continuing a recent surge of arrivals from West African countries to the Spanish archipelago, where the authorities declared a migration emergency earlier this week.

results.title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
results.content: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. The embattled government earlier announced it was pulling back its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend its temporary capital on the southern coast of Yemen.

results.title: Prague's fight for public TV: Why a high-profile presenter is prepared to walk away
results.content: Daniel Stach, one of the Czech Republic’s best-known television presenters and science journalists, tells Gavin Lee on France 24 why he is prepared to walk away from his career rather than work under changes he believes threaten the independence of public broadcasting.

results.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after 'sabotage' attempt at drone factory
results.content: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its ​foreign minister ‌said on Sunday, following a suspected ⁠sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blamed on ‌Moscow.

results.title: How did over 2,000 migrants reach the Canaries in just 48 hours?
results.content: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The strip of the Atlantic Ocean between West Africa and the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes – and the journey is usually made with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.

results.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
results.content: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

results.title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships in midterm elections
results.content: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee welcomes Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor to discuss the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children.

results.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
results.content: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

results.title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
results.content: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

results.title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
results.content: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days' time, where he is due to meet President Putin and President Xi. But there could be one fewer tech giant at the table: Jensen Huang, who has resigned from Nvidia amid a suspected espionage affair.

results.title: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
results.content: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

results.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
results.content: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.
